questions.question: A server alternates between up periods with mean time to fail $m_f$ and repairs with mean duration $\mathbb{E}[R]$. What does its availability $A=\frac{m_f}{m_f+\mathbb{E}[R]}$ measure?
options: The long-run number of failures per unit of up time.
The probability that a given job is finished without a failure.
The long-run fraction of time the server is up.
The long-run fraction of time the server is busy with jobs.

questions.question: For a server with failure rate $\lambda_f>0$ (mean time to fail $m_f=1/\lambda_f$) and mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]\ge0$, which statement about the range of the availability $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}$ is correct?
options: $0\le A\le1$, and $A=0$ when $\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]=1$.
$0<A<1$, since a finite $m_f$ means the server fails at some point.
$\tfrac{1}{2}\le A\le1$, since up periods last at least as long as repairs.
$0<A\le1$, and $A=1$ exactly when $\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]=0$.

questions.question: A server with failure rate $\lambda_f$ and mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]$ has availability $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}$. A redesign doubles the failure rate and halves the mean repair time. What happens to $A$?
options: $A$ decreases, because the server now fails twice as often.
$A$ stays the same, because $\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]$ does not change.
$A$ increases, because each repair now takes half as long.
$A$ changes, while the mean effective service time stays the same.

questions.question: A server fails at rate $\lambda_f$ and its repair times are exponential with mean $\mathbb{E}[R]$. They are replaced by deterministic repairs of the same length $\mathbb{E}[R]$, with $\lambda_f$ unchanged. What happens to the availability $A$?
options: $A$ increases, because the repair times are now less variable.
$A$ decreases, because most exponential repairs are shorter than the mean.
$A$ is unchanged, because it depends on the repairs only through $\mathbb{E}[R]$.
$A$ cannot be computed, because $\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}$ needs exponential repairs.

questions.question: A machine has mean time to fail $m_f=8$ hours and mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]=2$ hours. What is its availability $A=\frac{m_f}{m_f+\mathbb{E}[R]}$?
options: $A\approx0.059$

questions.question: A machine fails at rate $\lambda_f=2$ per day of operation, and a repair takes $\mathbb{E}[R]=4$ hours on average. What is its availability $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}$?
options: $A\approx0.111$
$A\approx0.923$
$A\approx0.667$

questions.question: In a single-server queue, failures occur only during service and a failed job resumes after its repair. The net service time has mean $\mathbb{E}[S_0]=12$ minutes and the availability is $A=0.75$. What is the mean effective service time $\mathbb{E}[S]$?
options: $16$ minutes
$9$ minutes
$15$ minutes
$4$ minutes

questions.question: A single-server queue has arrival rate $\lambda=2$ jobs per hour and mean net service time $\mathbb{E}[S_0]=0.25$ hours. The server fails only during service and has availability $A=0.8$. What is the load $\rho$?

A server alternates up periods $Z_k$ (mean $m_f$) and repairs $R_k$ (mean $\mathbb{E}[R]$); the $k$th repair ends at time $T_k$. Which choice of cycles and reward in the renewal reward theorem gives the long-run fraction of time the server is up?
options: Cycles $(T_{k-1},T_k]$, the reward is the up time; the fraction is $\mathbb{E}[Z]/\mathbb{E}[R]$.
Cycles $(T_{k-1},T_k]$, the reward is $1$ per cycle; the fraction is $1/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$.
Cycles $(T_{k-1},T_k]$, the reward is the repair time; the fraction is $\mathbb{E}[R]/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$.
Cycles $(T_{k-1},T_k]$, the reward is the up time; the fraction is $\mathbb{E}[Z]/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$.

questions.question: For a server with failure rate $\lambda_f$, mean time to fail $m_f=1/\lambda_f$ and mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]$, the availability is $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}$. What does the dimensionless product $\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]$ measure?
options: The expected repair time per unit of up time.
The long-run fraction of time the server is under repair.
The expected number of failures during one repair.
The factor by which failures multiply the mean service time.

questions.question: In a queue whose server fails only while a job is in service (failure rate $\lambda_f$ per unit of service) and resumes the job after a repair of mean $\mathbb{E}[R]$, a job with net service time $S_0$ has effective service time $S$. Which reading of $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}=\frac{\mathbb{E}[S_0]}{\mathbb{E}[S]}$ is correct?
options: A fraction $A$ of the jobs is served without a single failure.
A job is interrupted on average $1/A-1$ times during its service.
Of the time the server spends on jobs, processing plus repairs, a fraction $A$ is processing.
$A$ is the long-run fraction of all time, idle time included, spent processing jobs.

questions.question: A machine always has work and runs whenever it is up. Its up periods have mean $m_f=3.5$ hours, so $\lambda_f=1/3.5$ per hour of operation, and repairs take $\mathbb{E}[R]=0.5$ hours on average. In the long run, about how many failures occur per $1000$ hours of real time?
options: About $286$
About $250$
About $125$
About $219$

questions.question: A server with failure rate $\lambda_f$ and mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]$ has availability $A=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R]}=0.8$. The mean repair time doubles while $\lambda_f$ stays the same. What is the new availability?

Two single servers get the same Poisson arrivals and the same net service times, and fail only during service with exponential repairs. Both loads are below $1$. Machine 1: $\lambda_f=2$ per hour, $\mathbb{E}[R]=0.25$ hours. Machine 2: $\lambda_f=0.5$ per hour, $\mathbb{E}[R]=1$ hour. Which comparison is correct?
options: Both have $A=\frac{2}{3}$; machine 1 has the smaller $\lambda_f\mathbb{E}[R^2]$, so it waits less.
Both have $A=\frac{2}{3}$ and the same load, so their mean waiting times are equal.
Machine 2 waits less, because it fails four times less often than machine 1.
Machine 1 has the higher availability, because its repairs are four times shorter.

questions.question: A machine alternates i.i.d. cycles of an up period $Z_k$ and a repair $R_k$, both random with finite means. To estimate the availability, a student averages the per-cycle fractions $Z_k/(Z_k+R_k)$ over many cycles. Which statement about this average is correct?
options: It converges to $A$, since each per-cycle fraction is an unbiased estimate of $A$.
It converges to $A$ provided the up periods $Z_k$ are exponential.
It converges to $\mathbb{E}[Z/(Z+R)]$, which generally differs from $A$.
It converges to a value that always lies below $A$, so it underestimates $A$.

questions.question: A machine alternates i.i.d. cycles of an up period $Z_k$ and a repair $R_k$ with finite means, but within a cycle a long up period tends to be followed by a long repair, so $Z_k$ and $R_k$ are dependent. Which statement about the long-run fraction of time up is correct?
options: It is below $\mathbb{E}[Z]/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$, since long up periods are paired with long repairs.
It is still $\mathbb{E}[Z]/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$; dependence within a cycle does not matter.
It is $\mathbb{E}[Z]/(\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[R])$ only if $Z_k$ is exponential; otherwise a correction appears.
It cannot be found from means, since renewal reward needs a reward independent of the cycle length.

questions.question: A single-server queue has arrival rate $\lambda=3$ per hour and mean net service time $\mathbb{E}[S_0]=0.2$ hours. The server fails only during service at rate $\lambda_f=0.4$ per hour of service, and repairs take $\mathbb{E}[R]=0.5$ hours on average. What long-run fraction of all time, idle time included, is the server under repair?

A single-server queue has $\lambda=5$ jobs per hour and mean net service time $\mathbb{E}[S_0]=0.15$ hours. The server fails only during service at rate $\lambda_f=0.25$ per hour of service. Which condition on the mean repair time $\mathbb{E}[R]$ keeps the load $\rho$ below $1$?
options: $\mathbb{E}[R]<60$ minutes
$\mathbb{E}[R]<37$ minutes, roughly
Any $\mathbb{E}[R]$, since $\lambda\,\mathbb{E}[S_0]=0.75<1$
$\mathbb{E}[R]<80$ minutes
